question_text: According to the course material, ECO 122 Principle of Economics II is a three-credit and one-semester undergraduate course made up of:
option_a: twenty-one units spread across fifteen lecture weeks
explanation: The course is three-credit with twenty-one units across fifteen lecture weeks.

question_text: According to the course material, the course developer and reviewer of ECO122 is:
option_a: Samuel Olumuyiwa Olusanya (Economics Department, National Open University of Nigeria)
explanation: Course developer and reviewer is Samuel Olumuyiwa Olusanya of NOUN Economics.

question_text: According to the course material, the course editor of ECO122 is:
option_a: Dr. Kazeem Ajide (Economics Department, University of Lagos)
explanation: Course editor is Dr. Kazeem Ajide of the University of Lagos.

question_text: According to the course material, ECO122 is basically an introductory course on:
option_a: Macro-economics
option_b: only microeconomics of a single firm
explanation: The course content is basically an introductory course on Macro-economics.

question_text: According to the course material, the term "macro" was first used in economics by Ragner Frisch in:
explanation: The term macro was first used in economics by Ragner Frisch in 1933.

question_text: According to the course material, credit for developing a general theory of income, output and employment in the wake of the Great Depression of 1929 goes to:
option_a: John Maynard Keynes
explanation: Keynes developed a general theory of income, output and employment after 1929.

question_text: According to the course material, macroeconomics studies the behaviour of the whole (aggregate) economy rather than:
option_a: individual economic markets (the domain of Microeconomics)
explanation: Macroeconomics studies the aggregate economy, unlike microeconomics.

question_text: According to the course material, factors analysed in forecasting national income include level of employment/unemployment, GNP, balance of payments position, and:
option_a: prices (deflation or inflation)
explanation: Prices (deflation or inflation) are among the major macroeconomic factors.

question_text: According to the course material, Keynes defined full employment as the absence of:
option_a: involuntary unemployment
option_b: only frictional unemployment of every kind
explanation: According to Keynes, full employment means the absence of involuntary unemployment.

question_text: According to the course material, the Keynesian concept of full employment involves reduction in the real wage rate, increase in effective demand, and:
option_a: inelastic supply of output at the level of full employment
explanation: Three Keynesian conditions include inelastic supply of output at full employment.

question_text: According to the course material, economic growth is defined as the process whereby the real per capita income of a country increases:
option_a: over a long period of time
explanation: Economic growth is a long-period rise in real per capita income.

question_text: According to the course material, microeconomics is the study of individual economic units whereas macroeconomics is the study of:
option_a: aggregates of an economy as a whole
explanation: Macroeconomics studies aggregates of an economy as a whole.

question_text: According to the course material, the central problem of microeconomics is price determination and allocation of resources, while the central problem of macroeconomics is:
option_a: determination of level of income and employment
explanation: Macroeconomics centres on determination of income and employment.

question_text: According to the course material, Marshall developed and perfected microeconomics, while Keynes developed macroeconomics as a distinct method; the transition started with:
option_a: the publication of Keynes's general theory
explanation: The transition from micro to macro started with Keynes's General Theory.

question_text: According to the course material, Keynes rejected the assumption of full employment of resources, especially of labour, regarding full employment as:
option_a: a special case; the general situation is one of under-employment
option_b: only always the normal capitalist case
explanation: Keynes regarded full employment as a special case; under-employment is general.

question_text: According to the course material, the performance of an economy is judged by the Gross National Product (GNP) and the objective of government is to raise:
option_a: the material wellbeing of the country
explanation: Government aims to raise material wellbeing; performance is judged by GNP.

question_text: According to the course material, national income accounting is the bookkeeping system a national government uses to measure:
option_a: the level of the country's economic activity in a given time period
explanation: National income accounting measures economic activity in a given period.

question_text: According to the course material, Gross Domestic Product is the market value of all the final goods and services produced in a country during a given period by all factors of production:
option_a: located within a country
explanation: GDP counts production located within a country.

question_text: According to the course material, unpaid house works are not counted in GDP; goods and services provided by the government are included as:
option_a: the government's cost of providing them
option_b: only market prices they do not have
explanation: Government goods without market value are included at the government's cost.

question_text: According to the course material, only final goods and services are included in GDP; intermediate goods used up in producing final goods are not counted so as to avoid:
option_a: double counting
explanation: Intermediate goods are excluded to avoid double counting.

question_text: According to the course material, newly produced capital goods (factories, equipment, machines) are classified as final goods for GDP so as to avoid:
option_a: double counting
explanation: Capital goods are treated as final goods to avoid double counting.

question_text: According to the course material, if grain worth N25 is milled into flour worth N50 then baked into bread worth N150, the contribution to GDP is:
option_a: N150.00 which is the market value of the loaf of bread, the final product
option_b: N225 by adding grain, flour and bread
explanation: Only the final product (bread N150) is counted.

question_text: According to the course material, GNP is GDP plus net factor income from abroad, written as:
option_a: GNP = GDP + (Nf)
explanation: GNP equals GDP plus net factor income from abroad.

question_text: According to the course material, Net National Product is gross national product minus depreciation:
option_a: NNP = GNP – D
explanation: NNP = GNP minus depreciation.

question_text: According to the course material, Disposable Income is Personal Income minus:
option_a: Direct Taxes
explanation: Disposable Income = Personal Income – Direct Taxes.
